12 Rules for Life: Jordan B. Peterson’s two-book “Rules for Life” pairing: 12 Rules for Life addresses living amid chaos; the sequel Beyond Order offers twelve further rules aimed at excess order and rigidity. Audible’s library card labels the first book under this series name even when only that title is owned.
Audible Original Stories: Audible’s branded short-story collection of Originals from established and emerging authors across genres, typically short enough to finish in about one to two hours. Not a single continuous narrative series.
Bobiverse: Dennis E. Taylor’s hard-SF series about software engineer Bob Johansson, whose consciousness is uploaded into a self-replicating interstellar probe. As Bob copies himself across the galaxy, the diverging “Bobs” explore, fight existential threats, and try to secure a future for humanity—mixing large-scale space opera with AI identity questions and dry humor.
Children of Time: Adrian Tchaikovsky’s Arthur C. Clarke Award–winning sequence about fallen humanity’s ark ships and the unexpected sapient life that arose from ancient terraforming experiments—beginning with uplifted spiders (Portiids) and expanding across later books to other species and lost colonies.
Dune: Frank Herbert’s six-novel Dune Chronicles, set in a feudal interstellar future centered on Arrakis, the desert planet that produces the spice melange. The saga follows House Atreides, religion, ecology, and power from Dune through Chapterhouse: Dune.
Dune 7: Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson’s two-book conclusion (Hunters of Dune and Sandworms of Dune) based on Frank Herbert’s unfinished “Dune 7” outline, following survivors aboard the no-ship Ithaca and the return of the thinking-machine threat.
DUNE: Caladan Trilogy: Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson prequel trilogy (The Duke of Caladan, The Lady of Caladan, The Heir of Caladan) set in the year before the original Dune, focusing on Leto, Jessica, and young Paul amid rebellion and intrigue.
DUNE: Legends of Dune: Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson trilogy set ~10,000 years before Dune, chronicling the Butlerian Jihad—humanity’s war against the thinking-machine empire Omnius—and the origins of major Houses and institutions.
DUNE: Prelude to Dune: Also called the House Trilogy: House Atreides, House Harkonnen, and House Corrino. Set decades before Dune, it traces young Leto’s rise, Corrino succession intrigue, and Harkonnen–Bene Gesserit conflict.
DUNE: The Schools of Dune Trilogy: Also known as Great Schools of Dune (Sisterhood of Dune, Mentats of Dune, Navigators of Dune). Set after the Butlerian Jihad, it follows the founding struggles of the Bene Gesserit, Mentat schools, and Spacing Guild Navigators under anti-technology pressure.
Dungeon Crawler Carl: Matt Dinniman’s LitRPG series in which Coast Guard veteran Carl and his ex-girlfriend’s cat, Princess Donut, survive an alien “Dungeon Crawler World” game show built from a mined Earth—leveling through deadly floors while fighting the Syndicate that profits from the crawl.
Expeditionary Force: Craig Alanson’s military space-opera about Joe Bishop and Skippy, an ancient, sarcastic Elder AI. After Earth is drawn into a galaxy-spanning client-species war, Bishop’s improvised “Merry Band of Pirates” hijacks alien tech to keep humanity alive—mixing special-ops action with running comedy.
Extreme Ownership: Leadership books rooted in U.S. Navy SEAL experience, beginning with Extreme Ownership by Jocko Willink and Leif Babin and continuing with The Dichotomy of Leadership (and later related titles under the same branding). Practical leadership principles framed through combat and business case examples.
Foundation: Isaac Asimov’s classic SF sequence about the fall of a Galactic Empire and Hari Seldon’s psychohistory plan to shorten the coming dark age via Foundations that preserve knowledge and guide civilization through crises.
Go the F--k to Sleep: Adam Mansbach’s satirical adult “children’s book” series of short, profane parenting rants—bedtime, mealtime, a second child, and later college send-off—illustrated for grown-up readers rather than kids.
Harry Potter: J. K. Rowling’s seven-book fantasy about orphaned wizard Harry Potter and friends at Hogwarts as they confront Lord Voldemort—school story, mystery, and coming-of-age themes across the wizarding world.
Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy: Douglas Adams’s comic science-fiction “trilogy in five parts,” beginning when Earth is destroyed for a hyperspace bypass and Arthur Dent hitchhikes the galaxy with Ford Prefect, Zaphod, Trillian, and Marvin.
Jack Reacher: Lee Child’s (later co-written with Andrew Child) thriller series about former U.S. Army Military Police major Jack Reacher, a drifting loner who walks into small-town and big-city crimes and refuses to look away. Mostly standalone novels with occasional multi-book arcs.
Maasverse , A Court of Thorns and Roses: Audible’s combined label for Sarah J. Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses (ACOTAR) romantasy—huntress Feyre in the faerie courts of Prythian—within Maas’s broader connected “Maasverse” (also Throne of Glass and Crescent City).
Murderbot Diaries: Martha Wells’s Hugo/Nebula-winning SF series narrated by Murderbot, a security cyborg that hacked its governor module and would rather watch media than deal with humans—yet keeps getting pulled into protecting them across corporate space.
One and Only Ivan: Katherine Applegate’s children’s/middle-grade One and Only sequence (Ivan, Bob, Ruby) about animals finding sanctuary and confronting captivity, grief, and belonging. The One and Only Ruby (Book 3) centers on young elephant Ruby preparing for a coming-of-age ceremony.
One of Us Is Lying: Karen M. McManus’s YA mystery trilogy set around Bayview High—gossip, secrets, and deadly games—beginning with four students suspected after Simon’s death and continuing through One of Us Is Next and One of Us Is Back.
Quantum Earth: Dennis E. Taylor duology (Outland, Earthside): university researchers open a portal to an uninhabited alternate Earth and, after catastrophe on our side, struggle to build and govern a refugee colony while new threats emerge.
Skink Series: Carl Hiaasen’s Florida crime-comedy novels featuring Clinton “Skink” Tyree, a feral former governor turned eco-vigilante. Double Whammy (first Skink appearance) pairs PI R.J. Decker with Skink in a bass-fishing murder and Everglades corruption case.
Sun Symbol Series: Scott Sigler’s modern-era Siglerverse duo EarthCore and Mount Fitz Roy: deep-mining expeditions chase unprecedented platinum deposits and awaken ancient guardians far below Utah and the Andes.
The Crypt: Scott Sigler military SF/horror about the PUV James Keeling, a dimensional-jump ship that drives crews toward hallucination, violence, and madness. Criminals and misfits serve two-year sentences aboard for a chance at absolution.
The Dune Sequence: Audible’s umbrella series listing that groups Frank Herbert’s originals with Brian Herbert/Kevin J. Anderson prequels and sequels (Legends, Schools, House/Prelude, Heroes, Caladan, Dune 7, etc.) into one storefront sequence—not a single author-intended continuous novel cycle.
The Expanse: James S. A. Corey’s nine-novel space-opera (plus novellas) about Earth, Mars, and the Belt colliding after the discovery of the alien protomolecule—following James Holden and the Rocinante crew from solar-system politics through the ring gates.
The Lord of the Rings: J. R. R. Tolkien’s epic fantasy (one work published in three volumes) in which Frodo and companions seek to destroy Sauron’s One Ring in Mount Doom.
The Remembrance of Earth's Past: Liu Cixin’s hard-SF trilogy (The Three-Body Problem, The Dark Forest, Death’s End) about first contact with the Trisolarans and humanity’s struggle under the “dark forest” logic of the cosmos. Audible also groups Baoshu’s authorized spin-off The Redemption of Time with this label.
The Silo Saga: Hugh Howey’s dystopian Wool / Shift / Dust trilogy: underground silo societies endure lies about a toxic outside world, while a prequel thread reveals how the silos—and the catastrophe—were engineered. Adapted as Apple TV+’s Silo.
The Targaryen Dynasty: The House of the: Penguin Random House series grouping for Targaryen/House of the Dragon–related titles, including George R. R. Martin’s Fire & Blood (Targaryen history from Aegon’s Conquest through the Dance of the Dragons era) and companion/illustrated volumes.
Toltec Wisdom: don Miguel Ruiz’s Toltec Wisdom / “A Toltec Wisdom Book” spiritual self-help sequence, led by The Four Agreements—four practical codes for personal freedom—and related titles on love, knowledge, and mastery.
We Were Liars: E. Lockhart’s YA Sinclair-family universe beginning with We Were Liars—Cadence’s return to Beechwood Island after a mysterious accident—with later related novels (Family of Liars, We Fell Apart) that share the world but can be read with spoiler caveats.
Wizarding World Collection: Audible’s storefront collection branding for Harry Potter main novels plus related companion titles under the Wizarding World label—not a separate story continuity beyond the Potter books/companions.
Words + Music: Audible Original series pairing musicians’ personal storytelling with exclusive or reimagined performances—intimate audio essays about craft and life rather than a continuous fictional plot.
